subject: maths
title: Mean, Median, Mode & Range
welcome_lead: Three averages and one spread. Choose the right tool to describe data.
meta_desc: Calculate mean, median, mode and range in this KS3 data adventure.
final_note: Excellent! Averages and spread are now in your toolkit.

concepts.def: Sum of values divided by how many values.
The middle value when data is in order.
The most common value in the data.
A typical or central value of a data set.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Add all values and divide by the count.

Data: 2, 4, 6, 8. Sum = 20. Count = 4.

Mean = 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

Data: 3, 5, 5, 7, 9. Already in order.

Median = middle value = 5.

Mode = most common = 5.

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
The mode is 3 because it's the middle value.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.

mcqs.q: What is the mode of the data set [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5]?
options: The mode is 3 because it's the middle value.
Both 2 and 4 — the data set is bimodal because two values occur most frequently.
There is no mode because no single value is the most common.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: 7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.
5, because that is the middle value.
